summary: This benchmark evaluates multi-block causal subspace interventions by maintaining a fixed 25-coordinate representation of single-letter identifiers across seven transformer blocks in Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and Qwen2.5-14B. The authors demonstrate 100% target reversal across 512 test pairs under learned partner interventions while establishing that random matched-norm edits produce zero reversals. The benchmarking methodology is well-controlled and documents precise software versions, hardware, and model revisions, though evaluation is limited to synthetic single-token completions.
strengths: Clean experimental design with rigorous negative and matched-norm random controls isolating the causal effect of the learned 25-dimensional subspace.
Comprehensive reproducibility metadata, including pinned model revision hashes, software library versions, hardware specifications, and exact sample indices.
Consistent demonstration of complete causal control across two distinct model sizes (7B and 14B) with large logit margin separations (+12 vs -12).
weaknesses: The evaluation task is narrow, restricted to stylized synthetic Python return statements with single-letter identifier substitutions, leaving generalizability to natural multi-token code unverified.
The intervention mechanism relies on knowing the exact token position and prespecified layer span, which limits immediate applicability to open-ended generation or variable-length contexts.
suggestions: Extend the benchmark to multi-token identifier substitutions and realistic AST structures with variable scoping.
Perform a layer-sweep sensitivity study to establish the minimal and maximal block spans over which the coordinate tunnel remains effective.

claims.text: Twenty-six letter indicators have 25 independent differences.
claims.source: Standard linear algebra; affine dimension of 26 one-hot categorical indicator vectors is 25.

claims.text: Earlier work on variable-width training uses a distinct mechanism that skips computation on absent coordinates and restores them on widening.
claims.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.02536 and literature on variable-width transformer architectures.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Finding Alignments Between Interpretable Causal Variables and Distributed Neural Representations
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Extends single-point distributed interchange interventions into an iterative, multi-layer coordinate 'tunnel' across seven consecutive transformer blocks.
